heading: ## Live-tree re-pin and entry-command monitor — round 17

findings.quote: | `tools/registry-check.py` | gate | `python3 tools/registry-check.py --rev REV [--registry PATH] [--tag TAG] [--json]` · `--selftest` | 0 every active row held · 1 a row differs · 2 registry invalid, rev unresolvable, clone failed, or `--tag` matches no row · 64 usage |
findings.why: At C0 that command has two further exit-2 causes the row's 'or' list does not name: (a) `--only <name>` matching no row — `REGISTRY_CHECK: could-not-evaluate (--only 'no-such-row' matches no registry row)`, rc=2, and `--only` is missing from the row's own synopsis although the tool accepts it (tools/registry-check.py:11-12 at C0); (b) an unusable scratch root, added by the very commit under test — `registry-check: could-not-evaluate: cannot create clone scratch under the scratch root: TMPDIR is not a usable directory: '/nonexistent/nope' (could-not-evaluate)`, rc=2, from `class ScratchRootUnusable` (tools/registry-check.py:757) raised by `strict_scratch_root()` (:769-770). Severity: nit, and the exit class (2) is unchanged, so nothing in the section is contradicted and no exit-1/exit-0 claim moves. Counter-reading, stated so the judge can weigh it: 'clone failed' is general enough to absorb a scratch-root refusal, and the row reads as a non-exhaustive summary, so a reader could still map both refusals onto exit 2 by class.
